results.snippet:
A technically minded operator: The deeper you are willing to go into workflow rules, Blueprints, and custom functions, the more Zoho repays your time.

## Pricing: more flexible than it first appears

Zoho CRM offers five tiers: a Free plan for up to three users with basic CRM functionality, Standard at $14 per user per month, Professional at $23, Enterprise at $40, and Ultimate at $52, all prices based on annual billing, as Siit’s 2025 Zoho review outlines. [...] - Pricing is genuinely competitive: Capterra’s Zoho CRM pricing page confirms that paid plans range from $14 to $52 per user per month, with a free plan for up to three users, making it one of the most affordable full-featured CRM options on the market. If you are comparing on cost alone, budget at the Standard tier and upgrade only when you hit a genuine workflow wall. [...] ### How does Zoho CRM compare on price to alternatives like HubSpot?

Zoho CRM pricing typically runs from $14 to $52 per user per month, while HubSpot’s plans start at $45 monthly and climb into the hundreds for advanced tiers. For feature-equivalent tiers, Zoho is meaningfully cheaper, which matters most for teams with more than five or six users.

results.title: A detailed guide on popular pricing models | Zoho Billing
results.snippet:
Per-seat, per-month software licensing is the textbook case. It could be a user, or an organization depending on what it serves primarily. For an example, look no farther than Zoho Billing's pricing plans, they are charged per organization, with further limits on capabilities provided.

### How do you operationalize unit-based pricing? [...] Stair-step pricing offers a set of fixed-price packages, each covering a range of usage or a set of limits, and the customer pays the price of whichever step they fall into. Unlike tiered pricing, nothing gets added up across slabs, so the customer is either on one step or on the one above it.

It gives the customer a predictable bill while giving you room to shape each package around the job your customer is trying to get done.

### Where you can see this in action [...] You will seldom find ramp pricing on a public pricing page, because it is negotiated contract by contract. It shows up most in multi-year enterprise software agreements, where a customer rolls a product out to one department first and the rest of the company later, and no one wants to pay full price for licenses that will not be used for months.

results.title: Zoho Workplace Pricing: How Organizations Can Save Money and Increase Benefits
results.snippet:
The price of Zoho Workplace Standard starts at ₹99 per user per month, while the price of Google Workspace Business Starter is ₹270 per user per month.

That makes Zoho a good choice for cost-conscious businesses.

### 3. What Do You Get with Zoho Workplace?

The concept of affordable price does not limit businesses to rely only on one or two basic tools.

Zoho Workplace integrates many productivity tools into one suite. [...] Instead of having to manage different tools for various workplace operations, businesses can have an integrated platform.

### 4. Why Does Pricing Matter More as Your Business Grows?

Imagine your organisation has 100 employees.

Here is an easy annual subscription comparison based on the plans discussed above:

Details/ Zoho Standard/ Google Starter

Monthly cost per user/ ₹99/ ₹270

Number of users/ 100/ 100

Monthly subscription/ ₹9,900/ ₹27,000

Annual subscription/ ₹1,18,800/ ₹3,24,000 [...] Higher full-suite plan/ ₹399/user/month (Professional)/ ₹1,080/user/month (Business Standard)

These prices are calculated on the basis of publicly available annual billing rates in India. There may be tax implications. Plan benefits and storage differ from each other, so businesses have to consider all of them before choosing one.

And that makes the difference quite noticeable.
